note_on_the_robustness_key: The head choice per encoder is unchanged: both encoders use noisy-OR. What changed on 22 October 2026 is which of them the lockbox is spent on. score_confirmatory.chosen_models reads chosen only, so the message-passing encoder is no longer a tested model and is scored by naming it to --models in a run declared outside the tested family. The owner's words: 'Defer it to robustness. I don't want it constraining things because this is more about mechanistically identifiably predictive nosology'. Recorded as decision 9.77, registered as tested_models and robustness_models.
source: The owner's decision, not a development reading: 'I guess we should drop the sigmoid head then'. Registered reason: only the noisy-OR head has modules that can be read as pathways, which is the study's purpose. experiments/choose_heads.py was not run and stays as a record.
note_on_the_lockbox_field: score_confirmatory.chosen_models compares this path with the lockbox being scored, to stop a head chosen on another lockbox's development set from being reused. No head was chosen empirically here, so the check has nothing to guard and the field only satisfies the contract. The check compares paths rather than the lockbox's SHA-256, so it would not notice configs/lockbox_v2.json being redrawn for v4 (decision 1.2).
note_on_floors: No floors are recorded here. choose_heads.py writes the floors it compared against, but no head was chosen empirically, and as of 15 October 2026 no magnitude floor is registered at all: the decision rests on the paired interval. The projected floors that would have applied to a head choice are 0.032 macro and 0.043 micro, not the 0.041 and 0.028 of the superseded second revision.
amended: 2026-10-22, the message-passing encoder moved from chosen to robustness
